fully_cited_clause.title: Non-Compete / Restraint of Trade
fully_cited_clause.original_text: Clause 2. Non-Compete and Restraint of Trade: Upon termination or expiration of employment for any reason, the Employee shall be perpetually restrained and prohibited from engaging in, working for, advising, or investing in any business or profession in the software, technology, or consulting sector anywhere in the world for a period of five (5) years.
fully_cited_clause.explanation: The clause prohibits the employee from engaging in, working for, advising, or investing in the software, technology, or consulting sector anywhere in the world for five years following the termination of employment. It imposes a multi-year, global restriction on professional activities across broad industry sectors.
fully_cited_clause.risk_reason: The clause is overly broad due to its worldwide geographic scope, lengthy five-year duration, and inclusion of multiple extensive industry sectors. This creates significant risk by severely limiting future employment and earning opportunities for the individual.

grounding_examples.text: Employee agrees that for a period of 3 years following termination for any reason, Employee shall not engage in, work for, consult with, invest in, or start any business operating in the technology or business sector anywhere in the country.
Employee shall not, directly or indirectly, work for any client, prospective client, competitor, vendor, or partner of the Company for 24 months post-employment, without geographic limitation.
Employer may terminate Employee's employment at any time without prior notice or severance pay, whereas Employee must provide 90 days prior written notice and pay a replacement fee.

In the event Employee terminates employment prior to completing 24 months of service for any reason, Employee shall pay Company an immediate punitive penalty of $50,000 as reimbursement for training and onboarding costs without proof of actual cost.

statutory_provisions.title: Agreement in restraint of trade, void
statutory_provisions.text: 27. Agreement in restraint of trade, void.—Every agreement by which any one is restrained from exercising a lawful profession, trade or business of any kind, is to that extent void. Exception 1.—Saving of agreement not to carry on business of which good-will is sold.—One who sells the good-will of a business may agree with the buyer to refrain from carrying on a similar business, within specified local limits, so long as the buyer, or any person deriving title to the good-will from him, carries on a like business therein, provided that such limits appear to the Court reasonable, regard being had to the nature of the business.

statutory_citations.title: Agreement in restraint of trade, void
statutory_citations.reason: Under ICA-1872-s27, Section 27 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872 provides that every agreement by which anyone is restrained from exercising a lawful profession, trade, or business of any kind is to that extent void, subject to Exception 1 saving agreements not to carry on a business within reasonable specified local limits where goodwill is sold.
statutory_citations.reason_hi: ICA-1872-s27, Indian Contract Act, 1872 की Section 27 के तहत यह प्रावधान किया गया है कि प्रत्येक समझौता जिसके द्वारा किसी को भी किसी भी प्रकार के वैध पेशे, व्यापार या व्यवसाय का प्रयोग करने से रोका जाता है, उस हद तक शून्य है, अपवाद 1 बचत समझौतों के अधीन है कि उचित निर्दिष्ट स्थानीय सीमाओं के भीतर एक व्यवसाय नहीं किया जाए जहां सद्भावना बेची जाती है।
statutory_citations.reason_ta: ICA-1872-s27 இன் கீழ், Indian Contract Act, 1872 இன் Section 27, எந்தவொரு சட்டபூர்வமான தொழில், வர்த்தகம் அல்லது எந்தவொரு வகையான வணிகத்தையும் பயன்படுத்துவதைத் தடுக்கும் ஒவ்வொரு ஒப்பந்தமும் அந்த அளவிற்கு செல்லுபடியாகாது என்று வழங்குகிறது, விதிவிலக்கு 1 சேமிப்பு ஒப்பந்தங்களுக்கு உட்பட்டு நல்லெண்ணம் விற்கப்படும் இடத்தில் நியாயமான குறிப்பிட்ட உள்ளூர் வரம்புகளுக்குள் ஒரு வணிகத்தை நடத்த வேண்டாம்.

tempted_raw_citations.reason: Section 27 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872 renders agreements in restraint of trade void. Post-termination non-compete covenants in employment contracts, such as this perpetual or 5-year global restraint, are impermissible and void under this provision.

Article 19(1)(g) of the Constitution of India guarantees the fundamental right to practice any profession, or to carry on any occupation, trade, or business, which informs public policy against oppressive post-employment restraints.

While Section 124 of the Indian Contract Act defines contracts of indemnity, enforcement of indemnity or forfeiture mechanisms linked to restraint of trade conflicts with the Supreme Court ruling in Percept D'Mark (India) (P) Ltd. v. Zaheer Khan (AIR 2006 SC 3426), which reaffirmed that any post-contractual non-compete restriction violates Section 27.
